name: What Is the Best Order for ADU Planning?

mainEntity.name: What is the best order to plan an ADU so I do not waste money on redesigns?
mainEntity.text: What is the best order to plan an ADU so I do not waste money on redesigns?

acceptedAnswer.text: To avoid redesign costs, homeowners should begin with the property itself rather than with finishes or inspiration images. The right sequence is site feasibility, budget discussion, preliminary layout, code and utility review, engineering, permit drawings, and then construction. This order helps identify constraints before the project becomes expensive. For example, setback issues, plumbing routes, grading concerns, or structural limitations can completely change the best layout. Once those realities are known, the team can choose finishes and details that fit the approved plan. A contractor who offers design-build coordination can be especially helpful because the same team can align budget, constructability, and permitting from the beginning. That reduces the chance of paying for drawings that do not translate into a buildable project.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best order is site review, feasibility check, layout concept, budget alignment, engineering, permit-ready drawings, and then construction. Starting with finishes or floor plans before confirming site constraints often leads to expensive revisions. Early coordination between design and build teams reduces waste and speeds up approvals.
